hierarchy.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: AWS IoT Resource Hierarchy
hierarchy.content: AWS IoT uses a hierarchical structure to organize devices: Thing Types (templates) define device categories, Thing Groups provide organizational structure, and Things represent actual devices. This hierarchy makes it easy to manage devices at scale, perform bulk operations, and inherit policies across your IoT fleet.
hierarchy.next: Let's create some sample resources to see this hierarchy in action

thing_groups.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Thing Groups - Device Organization
thing_groups.content: Think of Thing Groups like folders for your IoT devices. They help you organize devices, run bulk operations, and inherit policies - all based on location, function, or whatever makes sense for your setup. Groups can even contain other groups, giving you tons of flexibility for large deployments.
thing_groups.next: Let's create some Thing Groups to organize our devices

things.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Things - Device Registration
things.content: Things represent your actual IoT devices in AWS IoT Core. Each Thing has a unique name, optional attributes (like serial number or location), and can be assigned to a Thing Type for consistency. Things are the foundation for managing devices, applying security policies, and syncing device state.
things.next: Let's create some Things with realistic attributes

relationships.title: 📚 LEARNING MOMENT: Thing-Group Relationships
relationships.content: When you add Things to Groups, you're creating organizational relationships that make bulk operations and policy inheritance super easy. A Thing can belong to multiple groups, and groups can be nested. This hierarchy is key for managing device fleets at scale and organizing devices by business logic.
relationships.next: Let's assign our Things to the right Groups
